findings.title: The independent max-count test has an impossible affected-row expectation
findings.body: Each table-driven subtest now creates and cleans up its own annotations, but this case creates 9 annotations with MaxCount=3 and still expects zero affected annotations. The cleanup should delete 6 rows in this isolated subtest, so the assertion at line 135 will fail (or, if altered to pass, no longer tests the intended second invocation behavior). Preserve state across two cleanup invocations in this case, or change the expected result and add a real repeat-run test.

findings.title: The change increases the frequency of every cleanup job by 10x
findings.body: Changing the shared cleanup ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute does not only affect annotation cleanup: it also runs temporary-file cleanup, snapshot/version/image deletion, invite expiry, short-URL deletion, and query-history retention/enforcement ten times as often. These jobs include potentially expensive database scans/deletes and filesystem operations, so this materially increases background load and changes their established scheduling behavior. Keep the existing global interval or schedule only the annotation cleanup at the higher frequency if that is required.

findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors with the full ID list
findings.body: Every successful batch emits an Error-level log entry containing the complete slice of selected IDs, and the corresponding completion entry does the same for each cleanup path. Batch size is configurable and the new test explicitly uses 32,767 IDs, so this can generate very large error log records and substantial logging overhead on normal cleanup runs, while also making monitoring report failures despite err being nil. Log only counts at Debug/Info level (and reserve Error for actual failures).
